body:
Global crypto market cap settled at $2.3T on July 24, down -0.85% over the past 24 hours, as the broad complex absorbed a mild but real risk-off tone. Total 24-hour volume came in at $62.7B, and the Fear & Greed index slipped further into fearful territory, printing 28 today versus 31 yesterday. The mood is best described as cautious consolidation rather than capitulation: BTC dominance held at 56.7% while ETH dominance compressed to 9.9%, suggesting capital is gravitating toward the relative safety of the largest asset rather than rotating into beta. The session has the feel of digestion after a constructive 7-day run, with most majors nursing modest losses and no single narrative driving outsized moves in either direction.

Bitcoin at $65,016 is essentially doing its job as the market's anchor, off just -0.20% in 24 hours and -0.30% in the last hour, with $25.66B in volume providing reasonable liquidity. The weekly print of +4.00% remains intact and that is the number that matters most for positioning. Per CoinDesk, BTC held near $65,000 even as an $800 billion AI-driven selloff rattled equity markets, which is a meaningful relative-strength data point. Bulls need to defend $65,000 with conviction; a clean hold there keeps the 7-day momentum story alive, while a break lower opens the conversation around the mid-$62,000 range. To the upside, $67,500 is the level that would attract fresh momentum buying and signal that the consolidation is resolved in favor of continuation. One headwind worth flagging: Bitcoin ETFs snapped a 7-day inflow streak with $225M in outflows according to CoinDesk, which removes a near-term tailwind and warrants close watching over the next 2 to 3 sessions.

Ethereum at $1,882.01 underperformed BTC with a -1.40% 24-hour decline and -0.40% in the last hour on $9.72B in volume, consistent with the ETH dominance compression noted above. CoinDesk specifically called out ether as part of today's pullback as investors digest tech earnings, and that thematic drag from the broader growth selloff is real. Among the altcoin complex, divergences are sharp. UNI is the standout, up +0.60% in 24 hours and +9.40% on the week, the only major in positive territory today and clearly benefiting from idiosyncratic DeFi flow. LINK is holding up relatively well at $8.5, off just -0.10% in 24 hours with a solid +4.40% weekly gain. On the other end, AVAX is being hit hard at $6.24, down -4.60% in 24 hours and -3.40% on the week, making it the worst performer across both timeframes and signaling something more than just broad market weakness. ADA at $0.166804 dropped -2.90% in 24 hours despite being up +5.70% on the week, while XRP at $1.11 fell -1.90%, with the latter's newsflow muddied by a 25% drop in RLUSD transfer volume even as Ripple launched its Mint institutional platform per Cointelegraph. DOT at $0.807689 is quietly deteriorating, down -1.30% in 24 hours and -4.70% on the week with only $0.07B in volume, a name to avoid on the long side.

Macro is driving the session's defensive posture on multiple fronts. The AI and tech equity selloff of roughly $800 billion in market cap created a cross-asset risk reduction impulse that crypto was not entirely immune to, even if BTC absorbed it better than most. On the regulatory side, the Clarity Act is expected to miss its window before Congress' summer break according to CoinDesk, removing a potential near-term legislative catalyst and extending the period of uncertainty for US market structure. Meanwhile, the EU has widened its Belarus ownership ban to cover all crypto service providers per Cointelegraph, a continued trend of jurisdictional tightening in Europe. Domestically, Bitcoin mining pool Poolin filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy per Cointelegraph is a minor but real signal of ongoing miner-side stress at current price levels. Against that backdrop, the ETF outflow data and a Fear & Greed index at 28 tell you that retail and institutional sentiment is fragile, not confident.

Watch 3 things closely into next week. First, whether the Bitcoin ETF outflow of $225M on July 24 proves to be a single-session anomaly or the start of a sustained reversal in institutional flows, because the 7-day run in BTC was in part built on that inflow streak and losing it changes the demand picture materially. Second, AVAX specifically deserves monitoring given its -4.60% single-day and -3.40% weekly print while peers recovered; if that underperformance deepens, it may signal a broader rotation out of layer-1 alternatives that could eventually pressure SOL and ADA as well. Third, the Clarity Act timeline is now a medium-term risk rather than a near-term catalyst, and any congressional leadership commentary that either extends or definitively kills the legislative window before the summer recess could move the market. A recovery in tech equities and a resumption of ETF inflows would be the clearest signal that the bull case is intact; a close below $65,000 on elevated volume would be the clearest signal to reduce risk.
